reference.source: WHO Classification of Tumours: Soft Tissue and Bone / Enzinger and Weiss's Soft Tissue Tumors
clinicalPearls: A rare sarcoma of uncertain differentiation that typically arises in the deep soft tissues of the limbs in adolescents and young adults
Often painless and slow-growing, so it may reach a considerable size or present first with metastasis before the primary is noticed
Highly vascular, and it has a notable propensity for early haematogenous spread to the lungs, bone and brain
Defined by a specific ASPSCR1-TFE3 gene fusion resulting from a translocation, producing strong nuclear TFE3 expression on immunohistochemistry
Histology shows the characteristic organoid or alveolar nests of large polygonal cells separated by delicate vascular septa
Diastase-resistant, PAS-positive intracytoplasmic crystalline material is a helpful diagnostic feature
Complete surgical resection is the mainstay for localised disease, while antiangiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitors and immunotherapy are used in advanced disease
reference.pathophysiology: Alveolar soft part sarcoma is a malignant tumour of uncertain lineage defined by an unbalanced translocation that fuses the ASPSCR1 gene to the TFE3 transcription factor gene. The resulting fusion protein acts as an aberrant transcription factor that upregulates targets including MET signalling and angiogenic pathways, driving the tumour's marked vascularity and metastatic propensity. Tumour cells are arranged in distinctive organoid nests separated by thin sinusoidal vascular channels, and the central cells characteristically lose cohesion to create the alveolar pattern. The rich vascular network underlies the tumour's tendency to disseminate haematogenously early in its course.
additionalInvestigations: MRI of the primary showing a highly vascular soft-tissue mass with prominent flow voids
Staging CT of the chest and imaging of bone and brain given the metastatic pattern
Biopsy with histological assessment of the alveolar nesting architecture
TFE3 nuclear immunohistochemistry and confirmation of the ASPSCR1-TFE3 fusion
PAS staining with diastase to demonstrate intracytoplasmic crystals
redFlags: Pulmonary, bone or brain metastasis at presentation
A deep, enlarging, hypervascular soft-tissue mass in a young patient
Late recurrence or metastasis many years after treatment of the primary
reference.prognosis: Alveolar soft part sarcoma is an indolent-appearing but ultimately aggressive malignancy with a high rate of late metastasis, and long-term survival is limited by distant disease even when the primary is controlled. Prognosis is more favourable when the tumour is small, localised and completely resected.
pitfalls: Mistaking the organoid pattern for metastatic renal cell carcinoma or paraganglioma
Being falsely reassured by slow growth and a painless mass
Failing to stage the lungs, bone and brain for occult metastasis
Not confirming the diagnosis with TFE3 immunohistochemistry or fusion testing
